column2: Paying 0.055 EUR per GB of traffic sent to French residents makes video streaming fundamentally unprofitable.

This is the most hilarious thing I have ever read. Part of me wants this law to go into effect just to watch an entire country send itself back to 1988 to try and compy with it.

Summary of n°I-1358:

- It's a tax on internet "content", but they haven't defined what that means exactly, so by default it would apply to all internet traffic.

- Bytes delivered to French users by ISPs are taxed (but not user uploads).

- ISPs are responsible for tracking exactly where every GB originates from and will have to report the names to the government.

- The "content provider" then has to pay 0.055 EUR per GB that they sent.

- No explanation for how user-to-user traffic is handled. No explanation for what ISP -> user means (e.g. does P2P count)? No details on how ISPs will track the upstream source. About a million other similar questions are unanswered.

- The amendment was adopted today, and the assembly will vote on it as part of their full budget (but there are still many stages left before it can become law). Even by government standards this is way too idiotic to actually come into effect.
Wait, why is VideoLan hit by this? Do they stream content themselves?

This is an exceedingly dumb tax. A more reasonable tax would be one for storing user data. That would make PII a liability, not something you hold on to forever in hopes of selling to some scammy third party when you fold.
They will tax everyone for everything before they even contemplate controlling their spending.

Here's a link to the amendment: https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/17/amendements/3210A/...

I don't have an X account, so I can't see the conversation, but there don't appear to be any carveouts for non-profits or small businesses in the amendment, unless perhaps "any company offering an internet access service to households and businesses" has more criteria in context than a simple reading would suggest.

I wonder how distribution via torrent would be accounted for. Or if it would be worth it for larger players to adopt such a model, or just pay up or exit France.
